cards.q: What does EtherChannel troubleshooting focus on?
cards.a: Why bundle members do not bundle. Causes include protocol/mode mismatch, inconsistent speed/duplex/VLAN config, or STP interference.

cards.q: What is the first command to check for EtherChannel state?
cards.a: show etherchannel summary, which shows the bundle state.

cards.q: In show etherchannel summary, what does the P state mean?
cards.a: The port is in the channel bundle (P = in bundle).

cards.q: What does the I and S state in show etherchannel summary mean?
cards.a: I means standalone (not in the bundle) and S means suspended. A member that will not bundle shows I or S.

cards.q: What does U in show etherchannel summary mean?
cards.a: The port is up and in the bundle.

cards.q: What must match across all bundle members?
cards.a: Speed, duplex, VLAN config (access or trunk), and native/trunk settings. Inconsistent members will not bundle.

cards.q: Which LACP mode combinations bundle and which do not?
cards.a: active/active and active/passive bundle; passive/passive never bundles. Similarly auto/auto (PAgP) never bundles.
A static bundle with no negotiation (no LACP or PAgP).

cards.q: What is the load-balancing behavior of an EtherChannel?
cards.a: The hash (based on src/dst MAC or IP) determines which member carries a flow, and traffic stays in order per flow. Verify with show etherchannel load-balance.

cards.q: How is an EtherChannel treated by STP?
cards.a: The bundle is one logical STP port, so a misconfiguration where members run STP separately means it is not a proper LAG.

cards.q: A suspended member is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: A configuration mismatch across the bundle members, shown with show etherchannel detail.

cards.q: Why might traffic not load-share across bundle members?
cards.a: The load-balance hash algorithm does not fit the traffic type. Fix with the port-channel load-balance command.
